Assembling Pittsburgh from it unchanged would have produced a candidate that rolled Indianapolis back from 82 published profiles to 67 -- two non-zero market deltas instead of one.

how_the_facts_were_derived.rule: Every published fact came from the repository's OWN reader (brightdata.policy_reading) run over the captured policy block, including every field it refused to derive. A promotion order is not the place to overrule a reader.

residence inn pittsburgh monroeville.why: The page states two fee expressions that do not reconcile: $25 per day per pet capped at $150 per month, and a $100 non-refundable fee per stay. The reader refused to choose, so the row publishes pets_allowed, weight and count with the fee withheld. This is why founder item PGH-R1-D1 does NOT block the promotion: the open question is which fee to publish, and no fee is published.

crowne plaza pittsburgh south.why: The page prints 'Pet weight limit: 100' with no unit. The reader refuses a unitless limit rather than assuming pounds.

beyond_the_observation_vocabulary.fee_tiers: The Hyatt row's banded fee is withheld by to_extraction as SCHEMA_CANNOT_REPRESENT because the observation format holds one amount, but the policy schema has carried fee_tiers[] since the migration and parse_stay_bands returns this ladder with an empty problems tuple (contiguous 1-6 and 7-30, both bases stated). PTF-MILWAUKEE-READER-TO-TIERS-034 exists for this gap and built the rungs.
beyond_the_observation_vocabulary.other_charges: Two rows state a SECOND labelled charge beside the first -- Courtyard Cranberry Woods a $20 per-night fee alongside its $75 per-stay fee, Hotel Indigo a $75 damage deposit alongside its $75 per-night fee. The single pet_fee slot cannot hold two prices, so the additional charge lives in other_charges[] with its own labelled quote. Neither charge is inferred from the other and neither is collapsed into it.

how_the_facts_were_derived.species: The Hyatt page says 'canine travel companions' and makes no statement about cats, so dogs are published as accepted and cats are left unstated rather than inferred.

defects_caught_before_assembly.what: Six of the eight new records carried the lowercase identity key in their display `name`, because the attended-capture artifact records identity SIGNALS and no display name, and the applier fell back to the key.
defects_caught_before_assembly.why_it_mattered: The join still worked, so no gate would have failed; eight public profiles would simply have rendered with a lowercase join key as their title.
defects_caught_before_assembly.fix: The display name is now read from the census canonical_name, and the promotion was re-run from a reverted base rather than patched in place.

defects_caught_before_assembly.what: The Hyatt row's pets_allowed quote was the two-word fragment 'Pet Friendly', lifted by the reader from the block's heading.
defects_caught_before_assembly.why_it_mattered: On the page that fragment is indistinguishable from the amenity chip this market's own capture contract promises never to publish as policy.
defects_caught_before_assembly.fix: That row now cites the property's own operative sentence, verbatim, and the applier refuses any pets_allowed quote that is not present verbatim in its own block. The Marriott and IHG rows were left alone: their 'Pets Welcome' / 'pets allowed' IS the label-value pair under the page's Pet Policy heading, which is what the market's other 53 records already cite.

defects_caught_before_assembly.what: A suspected U+FFFD corruption in the Hyatt night-range dashes.
defects_caught_before_assembly.outcome: NOT a defect. The stored character is U+2013 EN DASH; the replacement glyph was this terminal's cp1252 rendering. A note added on the false assumption was removed.

address_completion_rereads.why: The exclusion contract requires a non-empty address (empty string counts as missing), and every one of this market's 53 existing seed rows carries one. Two promoted rows rendered no street in their 2026-09-04 capture, and neither the census nor the shadow recensus held one.
address_completion_rereads.authorisation: The operator ruled in-conversation on 2026-09-05 that completing an approved row's required identity field with one free re-read is completion, not new acquisition. The first re-read was ruled explicitly; the second was applied on the same principle and is reported here rather than assumed.
